title: Israel’s destruction of Gaza has created a ‘toxic wasteland’, experts find
content:
Scientific and satellite findings warn of widespread contamination in Gaza, posing grave threats to public health ‘for generations to come’

Israel’s destruction of Gaza has left a devastating environmental legacy with poisoned water, contaminated soil and toxic air threatening the life-support systems that the population depends on for survival, according to a report.

Israel’s military assault has created widespread contamination across the entire strip, the report by Oxfam and the Conflict and Environment Observatory (Ceobs) finds, with heavy metals, explosive residues, asbestos from destroyed buildings, and sewage making the air, soil and water dangerous for Palestinians for decades to come.
snippet: Scientific and satellite findings warn of widespread contamination in Gaza, posing grave threats to public health ‘for generations to come’

title: Cop31’s big fossil fuel failure – podcast
content:
Delegates will begin to depart Turkey without a clear deal from the latest Cop31 talks on climate change.

With one key phrase, fossil fuels, missing entirely from the proposed final agreement, advocates, media and frontline nations have been left asking if these talks can still bring any real change to the climate front.

Environment and climate correspondent Graham Readfearn joins Nour Haydar to unpick the longest Cop meeting in history

Read more:

Cop31 climate talks break down as key deal rejected

title: UK and France believed to have vetoed UAE choice for UN secretary general
content:
Costa Rican diplomat remains frontrunner but needs to win over two more permanent members of security council

The UK and France are believed to have effectively vetoed a controversial United Arab Emirates diplomat in a vote for the next UN secretary general, ostensibly over the UAE’s alleged links to atrocities in Sudan.

The search for a new chief diplomat for the world remained deadlocked on Friday after the UN security council’s ninth straw poll once again did not settle on a candidate.
snippet: Costa Rican diplomat remains frontrunner but needs to win over two more permanent members of security council
creator: Ben Doherty in New York

title: US reacts cautiously to Myanmar genocide ruling as EU praises ‘critical’ role of UN’s top court
content:
Reactions to ICJ ruling underline global divisions over court with China raising concerns about judicial overreach

The US has greeted with caution the world’s highest court’s ruling that Myanmar committed genocide against its Rohingya minority, while China has raised concerns of judicial overreach.

Reactions to Thursday’s historic ruling underlined deep international division over the role of the court and similar institutions. The international court of justice (ICJ) had never previously found a state responsible for genocide and the decision could set a precedent for future genocide claims, notably a case against Israel.
snippet: Reactions to ICJ ruling underline global divisions over court with China raising concerns about judicial overreach

title: Race to be next UN secretary general exposes divisions among world powers
content:
Debate about dominance of permanent five members could reignite if major powers block Costa Rican frontrunner

The race to become the next UN secretary general could reach a decisive moment on Friday when a UN security council vote is likely to reveal whether the Costa Rican frontrunner for the post would be blocked by the big powers. If so, the setback will reignite a debate about the dominance of the permanent five (P5) members at the United Nations.

Rebeca Grynspan, an economist and UN insider who is from a family of Polish-Jewish wartime refugees to Costa Rica, has been in the lead in all but one of the eight straw polls of the 15 UN security council members since the first secret ballot was held on 30 July. Each member goes down the list of candidates, casting an “encourage”, “discourage” or “no opinion” vote for each candidate.
snippet: Debate about dominance of permanent five members could reignite if major powers block Costa Rican frontrunner
creator: Patrick Wintour Diplomatic Editor

title: UN warns against misuse of security laws as UK weighs Palestine Action ban
content:
Human rights committee publishes guidance on freedom of association, which criticises vague laws targeting ‘extremism’

The UN human rights committee has warned against the misuse of counter-terrorism and national security legislation as the UK’s highest court considers the lawfulness of the ban on Palestine Action.

In its first comprehensive guidance on freedom of association, the committee criticises vaguely worded laws targeting “extremism” or “undesirable” organisations.
snippet: Human rights committee publishes guidance on freedom of association, which criticises vague laws targeting ‘extremism’
creator: Haroon Siddique Legal affairs correspondent

title: IPCC report delay will threaten global effort to tackle climate crisis, says top scientist
content:
Johan Rockström, one of world’s leading climate experts, says slowing down scientific work puts cooperation at risk

Climate science is “foundational” to the Paris agreement and worldwide progress on tackling global heating, and attempts to delay new scientific reports threaten global cooperation on tackling the crisis, one of the world’s leading climate scientists has warned.

Johan Rockström, the director of the Potsdam Institute for Climate Impact Research, said the world’s leading body of climate scientists, the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change, must be allowed to work as quickly as possible on its next comprehensive assessment of global knowledge of the climate systems.
snippet: Johan Rockström, one of world’s leading climate experts, says slowing down scientific work puts cooperation at risk

title: One in four women globally unable to refuse sex within marriage, says UN
content:
Almost half of women in west and central Africa cannot withhold consent, with girls worst affected, UNFPA finds

One in four women around the world have no power of consent if their husband or partner demands sex, according to a UN report.

In west and central Africa, almost half of women (45%) are not able to say no in their own marriage, while a third of women (33%) in east and southern Africa and in Arab states face the same predicament. In Latin America and the Caribbean, one in 10 women are not able to refuse sex, said the report by the UN Population Fund (UNFPA) published on Thursday.
snippet: Almost half of women in west and central Africa cannot withhold consent, with girls worst affected, UNFPA finds

title: World ‘held hostage by oil mafia’, says Panama minister at Cop 31
content:
Key issues unresolved as summit enters final days, with 30 countries signed up to forge fossil fuel treaty separate to UN process

The world is “being held hostage by the petroleum mafia” and seems unable to break free, Panama’s environment minister has warned, as key issues remain unresolved in the final days of the UN Cop31 climate summit.

“We are in love with our kidnappers,” said Juan Carlos Navarro, at a press conference to announce 30 countries were now signed up to forge a new fossil fuel treaty, separate to the UN process. “We love the petroleum guys. We can’t live without them, and they are so smart they have convinced us that they are doing this for our own good.”
snippet: Key issues unresolved as summit enters final days, with 30 countries signed up to forge fossil fuel treaty separate to UN process

title: Fears grow that US will put Nobel-winning judge under sanctions after Myanmar genocide ruling
content:
A ruling against Myanmar could set precedent for court’s judgment on Israel’s actions in Gaza

Fears are growing that the US could impose sanctions on judges at the international court of justice, including this year’s Nobel peace prize winner, Navi Pillay, if the court rules on Thursday that the Myanmar government committed genocide against the Rohingya.

The ICJ has never found a state responsible for committing genocide, and a significant factor in previous cases has been how to prove “intent” in a crime defined as acts committed with the “intent to destroy, in whole or in part” a national, ethnical, racial or religious group.
snippet: A ruling against Myanmar could set precedent for court’s judgment on Israel’s actions in Gaza

title: Children at risk as ‘weaponisation of aid’ surges in conflict zones, analysis finds
content:
New assessment shows large increase in cases where access to humanitarian help is deliberately restricted, with most incidents in Palestine

The “weaponisation” of aid is becoming normalised, with new analysis revealing that deliberate holding back of humanitarian help to children in conflict zones has increased 16-fold in the past decade.

The assessment of UN-verified incidents corroborates concerns that denying vital aid is becoming a common tactic of modern warfare.
snippet: New assessment shows large increase in cases where access to humanitarian help is deliberately restricted, with most incidents in Palestine
creator: Mark Townsend

title: The Guardian view on climate and debt: a vicious cycle the world must break at Cop31 | Editorial
content:
Poor countries are paying creditors instead of preparing for climate disasters. The international financial system must stop deepening their vulnerability

The catastrophe that struck Nepal’s Himalayas in August began with a collapsing glacier. An avalanche of ice and rock unleashed deadly floods, sweeping away villages, bridges and roads, and leaving thousands dead or missing. It illustrated the dangers posed by global heating to the Himalayas’ increasingly unstable glaciers. Nepal lost a tenth of its electricity generation. Reconstruction will cost about $5bn. Yet the Loss and Damage Fund, hailed as a historic breakthrough at the 2022 UN climate summit, has earmarked just $20m for Nepal – less than 5% of the $482m that Kathmandu must pay its external public creditors this year.
snippet: Poor countries are paying creditors instead of preparing for climate disasters. The international financial system must stop deepening their vulnerability
creator: Editorial

title: Fifa accused of climate ‘record of failure’ due to Aramco deal and tournament expansion
content:
• Groups question ‘sincerity’ to meet emissions pledges

    • Groups question ‘sincerity’ to meet emissions pledges

  • Oil giant is a major sponsor of football governing body

    • Oil giant is a major sponsor of football governing body

    The United Nations has been asked to review Fifa’s status as a signatory to a key environmental initiative, with complainants arguing football’s governing body has a “record of failure” on climate action.

    Fifa is a signatory to the UN’s Sports for Climate Action Framework, a coalition which seeks to persuade sporting organisations to “work together to achieve a climate-resilient future”. Under the framework, signatories agree to cut their greenhouse gas emissions by 50% by 2030 and to “partner with key stakeholders to deliver joint climate action”. They can have their status as a signatory removed, however, if “sincerity in participation or ability to participate is a cause for concern”.
